FDR-Based Variable Screening via Univariate Cox Models

Source: R/screen_fdr.R
screen_fdr.Rd

Screens candidate covariates for a right-censored outcome by fitting a univariate Cox model \(\lambda(t \mid X_j) = \lambda_0(t)\exp(\beta_j X_j)\) per covariate, Wald-testing \(H_0: \beta_j = 0\), and controlling the false discovery rate (FDR) across all tests via the Benjamini-Hochberg (1995) step-up procedure.

Usage

screen_fdr(formula, data, alpha = 0.1, minscreen = 5)

Arguments

formula

A model formula with a Surv(time, status) outcome on the left-hand side and candidate screening covariates on the right-hand side (as used throughout survalis, e.g. fit_coxph).

data

A data.frame containing the variables in formula.

alpha

Target FDR level in (0, 1). Covariates with BH-adjusted p-value (q-value) <= alpha are retained. Default 0.1.

minscreen

Minimum number of covariates to retain. If fewer than minscreen covariates pass the FDR threshold, the smallest-p-value covariates are added back until minscreen is reached (subject to the number of candidate covariates available). Default 5.

Value

A character vector of selected covariate names, with an attribute "screen_table" holding the full data.frame of feature, p_value, q_value, and selected.

Details

For each candidate covariate \(X_j\), survalis fits coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ X_j, data = data) and extracts the Wald p-value for \(\beta_j\). Raw p-values \(p_1, \dots, p_p\) are ordered \(p_{(1)} \le \cdots \le p_{(p)}\) and the BH-adjusted q-value for the \(k\)-th smallest p-value is $$q_{(k)} = \min_{k \le l \le p} \left\{ \frac{p \cdot p_{(l)}}{l} \right\},$$ guaranteeing \(\mathrm{E}[\text{FDR}] \le \alpha\) under the retained set \(\{j : q_j \le \alpha\}\) (Benjamini and Hochberg 1995).

References

Benjamini Y, Hochberg Y (1995). "Controlling the False Discovery Rate: A Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing." Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 57(1), 289-300.

Examples

selected <- screen_fdr(Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + diagtime + prior,
                       data = veteran, alpha = 0.2, minscreen = 2)
selected
#> [1] "diagtime" "karno"   
#> attr(,"screen_table")
#>    feature      p_value      q_value selected
#> 1      age 4.329948e-01 4.759247e-01    FALSE
#> 2 diagtime 3.107793e-01 4.759247e-01     TRUE
#> 3    karno 4.513209e-11 1.805284e-10     TRUE
#> 4    prior 4.759247e-01 4.759247e-01    FALSE
attr(selected, "screen_table")
#>    feature      p_value      q_value selected
#> 1      age 4.329948e-01 4.759247e-01    FALSE
#> 2 diagtime 3.107793e-01 4.759247e-01     TRUE
#> 3    karno 4.513209e-11 1.805284e-10     TRUE
#> 4    prior 4.759247e-01 4.759247e-01    FALSE
